The 3 `viewport` commands of the editor at engine `319075e3f92b`: each with its description, its kind, the MCP toolsets that offer it, its parameters and their JSON Schema (the other groups have files of their own).

## viewport.capture

Renders the scene on the next frame and returns the picture as a PNG image, with its width and height. By default it looks like the viewport: its size (1280x720 while the viewport is hidden), the scene's primary camera while playing (the editor camera otherwise) and the editor overlays (grid, selection outline, light/camera/collider shapes) for the editor camera; camera &quot;scene&quot; takes the Game view's size when it keeps an aspect ratio or a fixed size (viewport.setSettings gameView). position, target and fov look through a camera of the capture's own (the editor camera with those changes; camera.get stays as it was): position + target looks from one at the other, either alone moves the editor camera's view keeping its direction; the result's camera is then &quot;custom&quot;, and view has the position, forward direction and fov used. With the editor camera outside play mode, a scene without any light of its own is lit by preview lighting (previewLighting: true in the result; the game will be unlit) and the game's screen-space text and UI canvases are hidden (hiddenScreenSpaceTexts and ui.hiddenCanvases count them): see viewport.setSettings, or use camera &quot;scene&quot; to see what the game shows. ui reports the game UI drawn: {canvases, hiddenCanvases, elements, drawCalls, pendingGlyphs}. Text and UI whose glyphs are still being prepared delay the picture by a few frames, so they are complete, and so do meshes, materials and textures of the view that are still loading (waitForAssets, default true: up to about five seconds of frames; waitedFrames counts the extra renders), and textures it draws that still lack the finer mip levels the view wants (up to about two seconds, as a texture budget may keep them out), and animators that animate only while seen (WhenVisible) until they show the pose of their time (a few frames, also while paused), and mesh renderers the scene just gained until they reached the GPU (a few frames for a million; renderStats.deferredInstanceBytes says what still waited), and the renderer's pre-exposure (the power of two its HDR values are scaled by, chosen from automatic exposure's metering read back frames later) until it settled (a few frames, also without waitForAssets; preExposureSettled false if it did not within 8), and a scene drawn with temporal anti-aliasing (PostProcess AntiAliasingMethod TAA), also without waitForAssets, until 8 frames of the complete view, the mean of its jitter's phases (temporalFrames: the frames the picture's history holds, 0 without it). Reports what was still loading when the picture was taken (pendingAssets), the textures drawn coarser than the view wants (texturesBelowWanted), animators drawn with an older pose (stalePoses), glyphs that could not be prepared in time (pendingTextGlyphs) and point and spot lights' shadow views not drawn (localShadowViewsPending; captures draw them all at once) and reflection probes whose capture was not loaded (reflectionProbesPending; waited for as assets are, with waitForAssets; captures convert loaded ones at once), and whether spatial screen-space reflections still lacked a previous frame's color (screenSpaceReflectionsPending). Every wait is bounded and the command succeeds when a bound runs out: complete is true when the picture lacks nothing, else incomplete lists the JSON pointers of the result's fields that say what it lacks (&quot;/pendingAssets&quot;, &quot;/preExposureSettled&quot;, &quot;/temporalFrames&quot; under TAA, &quot;/debugView/shadows/complete&quot;, &quot;/notice&quot; when the view fell back to another camera, ...). debugView colors the picture by streaming state, level of detail, mip levels, motion or shadow texels, or shows a lighting view (default: the viewport's, viewport.setSettings) and the result's debugView says what it found: {view, tintedEntities, pendingEntities, failedEntities, placeholderBoxes, entitiesPerLOD: \[LOD0, LOD1, LOD2, LOD3+\], lodErrorPixels: \[the largest error drawn at each of those, in pixels, where levels are chosen by their errors; else 0\], entitiesPerMipShortfall: \[at the wanted level, 1 level coarser, 2, 3+ or loading\]} among the entities in view; with &quot;shadows&quot; also shadows: {complete, shadowMapSize, surfaceShare, skyShare, uncoveredShare (of the image), median/p10/p90PixelsPerTexel, aboveFourShare (of covered receivers), cascades: \[{index, near, far, texelSize, screenShare, median/p10/p90PixelsPerTexel, aboveFourShare}\]}; with a lighting view debugView.lighting holds what it measured (EV100 percentiles, albedo shares, sunToSkyRatio). renderStats is what the captured frame drew, as editor.perf's renderStats (draws, instances, shadow casters, triangles, proxies, lights, timings), with gpuMs: the GPU's milliseconds per stage of the captured frame (empty, with gpuStatsFrame null, where the GPU writes no timestamps). quality draws the picture at a preset (default: the view's); renderStats.quality says what it drew with. Needs a GPU (fails in editors started with --no-gpu). live: true renders nothing: it reads back what the Scene view (camera &quot;editor&quot;) or the Game view (&quot;scene&quot;) presented, as it played, to see motion (trails, smearing, crawling) at exact steps: arm it after play.start {paused: true}, then run input.sequence or play.step. It fails when the view does not render, play stops or step atFixedStep already ran; images: \[{fixedSteps, temporalFrames, width, height, path}\]. renderer switches techniques of the renderer for this one picture, to show what they do (SpecularAntiAliasing, SpecularEnergyCompensation, DitherOutput, GPUDriven, OcclusionCulling, SpatialReflectionResolve, FXAASubpixel 0.75, GlobalIlluminationBounceGain 0 for one bounce, ...): it renders through a renderer of its own, so no view of the editor or game frame changes; the result's renderer echoes the switches set.

Unset ones keep the capture's own values. Automatic exposure meters each capture alone: compare switches that change the light with a fixed exposure. |
| `renderer.BatchAcrossMaterials` | boolean | no |   | Instances of a mesh share draws whatever their materials (false: the CPU path splits them by material). |
| `renderer.DitherOutput` | boolean | no |   | The 8-bit output is dithered (false shows the banding of gradients). |
| `renderer.FXAASubpixel` | number | no |   | FXAA's sub-pixel aliasing removal: 0.25 (the default) or 0.75. One of: `0.25`, `0.75`. |
| `renderer.FadeLevelsOfDetail` | boolean | no |   | Levels of detail cross-fade over a few frames instead of switching (captures: off). |
| `renderer.GPUDriven` | boolean | no |   | The GPU-driven path where the device has it (true, the default) or the CPU path (false). |
| `renderer.GlobalIlluminationBounceGain` | number | no |   | The share of last frame's light global illumination bounces again (1, the default; 0: one bounce). Value: at least `0.0`, at most `1.0`. |
| `renderer.HorizonFade` | boolean | no |   | Reflections a normal map turns into the surface fade out. |
| `renderer.OcclusionCulling` | boolean | no |   | GPU-driven frames leave out what lies behind what the view draws. |
| `renderer.SpatialReflectionResolve` | boolean | no |   | Spatial screen-space reflections are resolved over 5x5 pixels (false: each pixel's traced reflection as the march found it). |
| `renderer.SpecularAntiAliasing` | boolean | no |   | Specular lobes widen by how much the shading normal changes across a pixel. |
| `renderer.SpecularEnergyCompensation` | boolean | no |   | Specular light is compensated for multiple scattering (false: the single-scattering lobe, darker on rough surfaces). |
| `renderer.TextureStreaming` | boolean | no |   | Textures stream at the levels the screen needs (false: every texture drawn is made resident whole). |
| `renderer.VisibilityFeedback` | boolean | no |   | GPU-driven frames take their asset requests from the GPU's visibility feedback. |
| `target` | array of number | no |   | Look at this point (a camera of the capture's own; the editor camera does not move). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `waitForAssets` | boolean | no |   | Render again on the following frames while assets of the view are still loading, up to about five seconds, while textures lack the mip levels the view wants, up to about two, and while new mesh renderers are on their way to the GPU (default true); false takes the picture at once. |
| `width` | integer | no |   | Image width in pixels; without height the viewport's aspect ratio is kept. Value: at least `16`, at most `4096`. |

## viewport.getSettings

The viewport's view settings (saved with the project's editor state): which editor overlays are drawn (grid, selectionOutline, sceneGizmos, stats; allColliders: collider shapes of every entity instead of only the selection's), previewLighting (editor views light scenes without any light of their own with a preview sun and sky), gameUI (editor views draw the game's screen-space UI, its HUD text and UI canvases, and a click selects a UI element), canvasMode (the 2D canvas mode for placing game UI), the gizmo mode and space, whether gizmo drags snap, the snap steps, debugView (&quot;none&quot;, or &quot;streaming&quot; / &quot;lod&quot; / &quot;mip&quot; / &quot;motion&quot; / &quot;shadows&quot;: the image colored by streaming state, level of detail, the mip levels textures lack, motion or shadow texels per pixel; or a lighting view: &quot;lighting&quot;, &quot;ao&quot;, &quot;indirect&quot;, &quot;luminance&quot;, &quot;albedo&quot;, or global illumination's &quot;voxels&quot;, &quot;gi&quot;, &quot;open&quot;, &quot;probes&quot;; &quot;specular&quot; and &quot;diffuse&quot; the light of one kind, &quot;clusters&quot; the lights each pixel's light cluster lists; &quot;culled&quot; boxes of what culling left out, &quot;wireframe&quot; the triangles' edges), gameView (the Game view's image: {mode, width, height}, width and height for mode &quot;custom&quot;), pilotGameCamera (the Scene view looks through the scene's primary camera) and editPose (&quot;rest&quot; or &quot;clipStart&quot;: what skinned characters of the edited scene show while it does not play).

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `viewport` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorViewportCommands.cpp:1101`

## viewport.setSettings

Changes view settings of the viewport (a view change: no undo step, the scene is unchanged) and returns all of them like viewport.getSettings. Editor views are the Scene view's editor camera (also while the game plays); the Game view and the scene's camera always show the scene as the game does.

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `viewport` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorViewportCommands.cpp:1118`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allColliders` | boolean | no |   | Draw the collider shapes of every entity; off (the default), only those of the selection and its descendants. |
| `canvasMode` | boolean | no |   | The 2D canvas mode (edit mode): the viewport shows the selection's UI canvas (else the first) at its reference aspect ratio through the scene's camera with the game UI, with handles to move and resize UI elements. |
| `cellBounds` | boolean | no |   | While a world is open (or the game streams one), draw the squares of its cells loading (Sulfur), loaded (Ochre) and unloading (gray) around the camera. |
| `debugView` | string | no |   | Color every view of the viewport: &quot;streaming&quot; tints entities whose mesh, material or textures are still loading (Sulfur; failed ones Cinnabar; entities whose mesh is not there are drawn as boxes), &quot;lod&quot; tints entities by the level of detail they are drawn at (0 to 3+), &quot;mip&quot; tints entities with textures by the mip levels their worst texture lacks against what their view needs (none Malachite, 1 Azurite, 2 Sulfur, 3 or more or still loading Cinnabar), &quot;motion&quot; colors every pixel by its motion since the view's previous frame (hue: the direction, right red, up yellow-green, left cyan, down violet; strength: the speed, full at 16 pixels a frame; still pixels darkened), &quot;shadows&quot; colors receivers by screen pixels per shadow texel (green at most 1, yellow 2, red 4 and more), outlines the sun's cascades and hatches their blend bands, &quot;lighting&quot; shades every lit surface white (the light alone), &quot;ao&quot; shows the occlusion that darkens indirect light (white: none), &quot;indirect&quot; only the sky's, probes' and reflected light, &quot;luminance&quot; the scene's luminance in EV100 bands (log2 nits + 3; the legend names them), &quot;albedo&quot; the base colors with values below 0.03 marked Azurite and above 0.85 striped Cinnabar, &quot;voxels&quot; global illumination's voxels: the scene as the GI sees it, each surface its voxels' albedo, two-sided voxels (no bounce) Cinnabar, &quot;gi&quot; global illumination's diffuse light on white surfaces (its field near the camera, today's light beyond), &quot;open&quot; the share of the sky each surface sees through the world as gray, &quot;probes&quot; its first cascade's probes, dead ones (inside solids) dark red, &quot;specular&quot; only the specular light (the lights' highlights and image light's reflections) and &quot;diffuse&quot; only the diffuse light, both without emission and fog, &quot;clusters&quot; how many lights each pixel's light cluster lists (bands: none, 1, 2-3, 4-7, ...; what its shading walks), &quot;culled&quot; the bounds of the mesh renderers in view that culling left out, as boxes over everything: Sulfur those too small on screen (grown to about 6 pixels across), Cinnabar those hidden behind what is drawn (occlusion culling, on the GPU-driven path only), &quot;wireframe&quot; the edges of every triangle drawn (all levels of detail, skins as posed) over the image, &quot;none&quot; shows the image as rendered. One of: `none`, `streaming`, `lod`, `mip`, `motion`, `shadows`, `lighting`, `ao`, `indirect`, `luminance`, `albedo`, `voxels`, `gi`, `open`, `probes`, `specular`, `diffuse`, `clusters`, `culled`, `wireframe`. |
| `editPose` | string | no |   | What skinned characters of the edited scene show while it does not play: &quot;rest&quot; (the default) their skeleton's rest pose, &quot;clipStart&quot; the first frame of what they play on start (the controller's default state's clip, else the Animator's Clip; the rest pose without either). animation.preview requests win over both, and play mode is unchanged. One of: `rest`, `clipStart`. |
| `gameUI` | boolean | no |   | Editor views draw the game's screen-space UI (its HUD text and UI canvases), and a click in the view selects a UI element; off by default so the HUD does not cover the scene. |
| `gameView` | object | no |   |   |
| `gameView.height` | integer | no |   | Height of the custom size. Value: at least `16`, at most `8192`. |
| `gameView.mode` | string | no |   | The Game view's image: free fills the panel, an aspect ratio is the largest image of it inside the panel (letterboxed), a size renders at exactly those pixels scaled to fit, custom uses width and height, game the resolution the running game asked for (free without a request). One of: `free`, `16:9`, `16:10`, `4:3`, `21:9`, `1920x1080`, `1280x720`, `custom`, `game`. |
| `gameView.width` | integer | no |   | Width of the custom size. Value: at least `16`, at most `8192`. |
| `gizmo` | string | no |   | Transform gizmo of the viewport. One of: `None`, `Translate`, `Rotate`, `Scale`. |
| `grid` | boolean | no |   | Draw the ground grid. |
| `pilotGameCamera` | boolean | no |   | The Scene view looks through the scene's primary camera, with the editor's overlays (F8). |
| `previewLighting` | boolean | no |   | Editor views light scenes without any light of their own (no directional, point, spot or sky light) with a preview sun and sky (never part of the scene or the game). |
| `quality` | string | no |   | What the Scene view draws with: the project's Graphics Quality (Renderer.Quality, the default) or a preset of this editor's for the view (a view setting, saved with the editor's state, no undo step); the Game view and the scene's camera always draw at the game's: the project's, and while playing the players' options over it. One of: `project`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`. |
| `rotateSnap` | number | no |   | Rotation snapping step in degrees. Value: at least `0.0`, at most `360.0`. |
| `scaleSnap` | number | no |   | Scale snapping step. Value: at least `0.0`, at most `100.0`. |
| `sceneGizmos` | boolean | no |   | Draw light, camera and collider shapes (far away lights and cameras as small icons). |
| `selectionOutline` | boolean | no |   | Outline the selected entities. |
| `snap` | boolean | no |   | Snap gizmo drags to the steps below (holding Ctrl inverts it). |
| `space` | string | no |   | Space the gizmo works in. One of: `Local`, `World`. |
| `stats` | boolean | no |   | Show frame time, draw calls and loading assets over the image. |
| `translateSnap` | number | no |   | Move snapping step in world units. Value: at least `0.0`, at most `10000.0`. |
